name: Magic Wand
tagline: Mouse, HUD, scrolling and speech to text from three buttons on a wand.
summary: Turning the wand moves my Mac’s pointer or the Agentic Mouse HUD outline. A Puck.js at the tip reads the rotation and sends it over Bluetooth.
status: Control V2 stops held scrolling and dragging on physical button-up or lost button telemetry. Recording and mouse lights are steady. Automated checks passed; physical acceptance is pending.
Wand Receiver has a menu-bar Options menu. Optional first-flick scrolling in V1 passes automated checks; physical gesture acceptance is pending.
Shared orientation correction and full Middle double-tap dismissal pass automated checks; physical acceptance is pending.
Held scrolling now stays locked until release; Bottom double tap recenters the pointer. Automated checks passed; these changes still need a physical check.
Ethan confirmed the latest native pointing feels much smoother; the other experimental gestures still need a physical check.
Held positioning clicks on release and resumes prior high sensitivity after 300 ms. Ethan confirmed the still-hand tolerance feels good.
Ethan confirmed automatic pickup and put-down both work on receiver 1.2.35.
HIGH dwell, held rough circles and VS Code review pass automated checks; physical acceptance is pending.
End-to-end latency, accuracy and battery life haven’t been measured.

parts: Puck.js v2.1: gyro, Bluetooth and an RGB light
hardware.wiring: Each button connects its pin to GND. The Puck’s internal pull-ups make a press read low.

buttons.name: Top
notes: Recording stays red when no other mode is active. Mouse mode stays blue, including while recording.

buttons.name: Middle
gestures: Open the HUD on Switch App, then turn the wand to move the outline
Use the outlined card on release
Hold the card; on some wheel cards, tilt to turn the wheel
notes: The outline stops at the edges instead of wrapping.
Bottom goes back to the pointer.

VS Code app mode: hold Bottom and tilt down or up to review changes. Crossed files are staged on release through Better Git. Double tap Bottom to toggle file staging mode; green is change review and purple is file staging.
The browser demo shows the main HUD; native app-specific controls and desk detection need the installed integrations.

buttons.name: Bottom
gestures: Click once after a 450 ms pause
Move up or down to scroll; release to stop
Drag with the mouse button down; release to drop
Recenter the pointer on the main screen and keep following
notes: Control V2 keeps short taps unchanged. The existing 220 ms cutoff separates a tap from a hold.
The target under the pointer at press chooses scrolling or native dragging. Scrolling stays in that area until release.
Flick and circular-scroll recognition are disabled in V2. Control V1 retains the earlier gestures.
VS Code app mode retains Bottom review controls.
Middle switches to the HUD. The pointer stays within real display edges.

chords.name: Bottom + Middle
gestures: Scroll sideways and up or down at once, including diagonals

lights.name: Updating
lights.detail: Receiver is updating the device code

lights.name: Calibrating
lights.detail: Keep it still with no buttons pressed for two seconds

lights.name: App review
lights.detail: Green for app review; purple for VS Code file staging

lights.name: Recording
lights.detail: Steady red while idle. Mouse, HUD and scrolling keep their own colours.

orientationCompensation.scope: Shared correction for mouse, HUD selection, held actions, review and scrolling. Wrist roll and elevated-tip heading correction run before screen-axis gains, with heading correction capped at 2x. No new movement buffer.

flickScroll.description: Optional: in HIGH mouse mode with Bottom released, flick up then lower slowly to scroll up. The pointer stays put during the gesture.
